body_text: View All News Waste Connections Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results and Raises Full Year Outlook July 22, 2026 Download (opens in new window) Better than expected results drive increase to full year 2026 outlook, with upside from improving commodities and ongoing acquisition activity Revenue of $2.562 billion, above expectations and up 6.4% Net income of $296.4 million, or $1.17 per share, adjusted net income* of $381.7 million, or $1.50 per share Adjusted EBITDA* of $840.1 million, above expectations and up 6.8% Adjusted EBITDA* margin of 32.8% of revenue Record year-to-date share repurchases of $614.5 million, or approximately 1.5% of shares outstanding TORONTO--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Waste Connections, Inc. (TSX/NYSE: WCN) (“Waste Connections” or the “Company”) today announced its results for the second quarter of 2026 and raised its outlook for the full year. “We are extremely pleased to deliver results above expectations, led primarily by strong operational execution driving a top-to-bottom beat in the second quarter. Most notably, adjusted EBITDA* margin expanded to 32.8% on 70 basis points of underlying margin expansion overcoming cost pressures primarily from rapidly spiking fuel and related costs, as well as ongoing drags from comparatively lower commodity values,” said Ronald J. Mittelstaedt, President and Chief Executive Officer. "Our outperformance, in spite of ongoing geopolitical instability and the associated uncertainty, is a reflection of our differentiated strategy and a purposeful culture, both of which will continue to set us apart." “Our achievements in the first half of 2026, with recent commodity values and ongoing fuel cost recovery, plus contributions from acquisitions closed to date, position us to increase our full year outlook to revenue of $10.02 billion to $10.05 billion and adjusted EBITDA* of $3.33 billion to $3.34 billion, with upside from improving trends in commodities and contributions from incremental acquisitions.” Mr. Mittelstaedt added, “Along with a record amount of share repurchases, we’ve completed acquisitions with over $100 million in annualized revenue and remain well-positioned for another outsized year of activity. The enduring strength of our balance sheet and free cash flow generation once again demonstrates our ability to fund our growth strategy while increasing our return of capital to shareholders.” Q2 2026 Results Revenue in the second quarter totaled $2.562 billion, up from $2.407 billion in the year ago period. Operating income was $437.6 million, which included $58.5 million primarily attributable to impairments related to adjustments to landfill closure and post closure costs and $7.9 million primarily in transaction-related expenses. This compares to operating income of $459.5 million in the second quarter of 2025, which included $7.3 million primarily in impairments and other operating items and transaction-related expenses. Net income in the second quarter was $296.4 million, or $1.17 per share on a diluted basis of 253.9 million shares. In the year ago period, the Company reported net income of $290.3 million, or $1.12 per share on a diluted basis of 259.0 million shares. Adjusted net income* in the second quarter was $381.7 million, or $1.50 per diluted share, versus $333.1 million, or $1.29 per diluted share, in the prior year period. Adjusted EBITDA* in the second quarter was $840.1 million, as compared to $786.4 million in the prior year period. Adjusted net income, adjusted net income per diluted share and adjusted EBITDA, all non-GAAP measures, primarily exclude impairments and acquisition-related items, as reflected in the detailed reconciliations in the attached tables. Six Months Year to Date Results For the six months ended June 30, 2026, revenue was $4.932 billion, up from $4.635 billion in the year ago period. Operating income, which included $138.0 million primarily attributable to adjustments to landfill closure and post closure costs, $9.9 million in transaction-related expenses, partially offset by $1.3 million in fair value changes to equity awards, was $801.6 million, as compared to operating income of $849.8 million in the prior year period, which included $27.5 million primarily attributable to transaction-related expenses and impairments and other operating items. Net income for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $515.7 million, or $2.02 per share on a diluted basis of 254.9 million shares. In the year ago period, the Company reported net income of $531.8 million, or $2.05 per share on a diluted basis of 258.9 million shares. Adjusted net income* for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $696.6 million, or $2.73 per diluted share, compared to $626.2 million, or $2.42 per diluted share, in the year ago period. Adjusted EBITDA* for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was $1.610 billion, as compared to $1.499 billion in the prior year period. Updated 2026 Outlook Waste Connections also updated its outlook for 2026, which assumes no change in the current economic environment or underlying economic trends. The Company’s outlook excludes any impact from additional acquisitions that may close during the year, and expensing of transaction-related items. The outlook provided below is forward looking, and actual results may differ materially depending on risks and uncertainties detailed at the end of this release and in our periodic filings with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and the securities commissions or similar regulatory authorities in Canada. Certain components of the outlook for 2026 are subject to quarterly fluctuations. See reconciliations in the attached tables. Revenue is estimated to be between $10.02 billion to $10.05 billion; Net income is estimated to be between $1.169 billion and $1.173 billion, and adjusted EBITDA * is estimated to be between $3.33 billion and $3.34 billion; Capital expenditures are estimated to be approximately $1.25 billion; and Net cash provided by operating activities is estimated to be between $2.63 billion and $2.68 billion, and adjusted free cash flow * is estimated to be between $1.40 billion and $1.45 billion. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- * A non-GAAP measure; see accompanying Non-GAAP Reconciliation Schedule Q2 2026 Earnings Conference Call Waste Connections will be hosting a conference call related to second quarter earnings on July 23rd at 8:30 A.M. Eastern Time. A live audio webcast of the conference call can be accessed by visiting investors.wasteconnections.com and selecting "Events & Presentations" from the website menu. Alternatively, conference call participants can preregister by clicking here . Registered participants will receive dial-in instructions and a personalized code for entry to the conference call. Shortly after the conclusion of the conference call, a webcast replay will be available on the Waste Connections investor website or by clicking here. About Waste Connections Waste Connections ( wasteconnections.com ) is an integrated solid waste services company that provides non-hazardous waste collection, transfer and disposal services, including by rail, along with resource recovery primarily through recycling and renewable fuels generation. The Company serves approximately nine million residential, commercial and industrial customers in mostly exclusive and secondary markets across 46 states in the U.S. and six provinces in Canada. Waste Connections also provides non-hazardous oilfield waste treatment, recovery and disposal services in several basins across the U.S. and Canada, as well as intermodal services for the movement of cargo and solid waste containers in the Pacific Northwest. Waste Connections views its sustainability efforts as integral to its business, with initiatives consistent with its objective of long-term value creation and focused on reducing emissions, increasing resource recovery of both recyclable commodities and clean energy fuels, reducing reliance on off-site disposal for landfill leachate, further improving safety and enhancing employee engagement. Visit wasteconnections.com/sustainability for more information and updates on our progress towards targeted achievement. Waste Connections defines adjusted EBITDA as net income, plus income tax provision, plus interest expense, less interest income, plus depreciation and amortization expense, plus closure and post-closure accretion expense, plus or minus any loss or gain on impairments and other operating items, plus other expense, less other income. title: Pixelworks to Announce Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results on August 11

Pixelworks (NASDAQ: PXLW) is a technology licensing company specializing in cinematic visualization solutions, including industry-leading content creation, delivery and display processing solutions that enable highly authentic viewing experiences with superior visual quality. Pixelworks has more than 20 years of delivering image processing innovation to leading providers of consumer electronics, professional displays and video streaming services. About TrueCut Motion TrueCut Motion is a powerful video platform from Pixelworks that provides filmmakers with a new palette for motion. It enables shot-by-shot motion grading, allowing creators to manage judder, motion blur, and frame rates to achieve a consistent, cinematic look across all screens. title: AIRE Launches Internal AI-Powered Engagement Assistant to Automate Lead Management and Streamline Mortgage Workflow
summary: reAlpha introduces its internal AI-Powered Engagement Assistant to automate lead qualification and improve borrower outreach, supporting faster, more efficient mortgage workflows.
body_text: AI-driven workflow automation improves mortgage operations by strengthening top-of-funnel conversion performance DUBLIN, OH – Nov. 17, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - reAlpha Tech Corp. (Nasdaq: AIRE) (“reAlpha” or the “Company”), an AI-powered real estate technology company, today announced the launch of its internal AI-powered Engagement Assistant, a multi-agent system designed to handle top-of-the-funnel lead qualification, appointment booking, and other pre-application workflows, helping improve scalability and efficiency across mortgage operations. Recent performance results [1] of the internal AI-powered Engagement Assistant have shown clear improvements across key front-end mortgage workflows. The system increased borrower lead engagement by more than 90 percent, improved appointment conversion by over 200 percent, and generated an increase of more than 140 percent in completed applications compared to manual outreach processes.[2] These results reflect the system’s ability to accelerate borrower’s connection to licensed loan officers for personalized support and maintain consistent follow-up for remaining prospects. The system is designed to provide timely, organized information to the sales team while preserving compliance and data integrity across communication workflows. The internal system works seamlessly within reAlpha’s customer relationship management system (“CRM”). A customer support assistant welcomes new prospects, assesses the borrower’s intent, answers routine inquiries that do not require a licensed mortgage professional, and organizes borrower information so licensed team members can respond efficiently. A loan application assistant guides early-stage borrowers through digital intake forms, capturing their key goals and application information. An appointment booking assistant schedules consultations for borrowers ready to move forward with the mortgage process, managing appointment confirmations, rescheduling, and follow-ups. These features are designed to work together to improve borrower engagement with the intent to reduce repetitive manual work for loan officers. According to a 2024 consumer survey, the first professional to engage a motivated borrower is most likely to win the business, reinforcing the need for rapid, consistent outreach.[3] An industry study shows that 78 percent of customers buy from the first company that responds to their inquiry,[4] and reaching out to a prospective borrower within five minutes can increase qualification rates more than twenty times compared to a 30-minute delay.[5] Research shows that more than 30 percent of inbound leads receive no follow-up,[6] resulting in substantial lost opportunity. reAlpha’s new system addresses this gap by automating initial screening and customer engagement, enabling timely outreach within regulated hours and ensuring that qualified borrowers are efficiently routed to loan officers. reAlpha’s use of the internal AI-Powered Engagement Assistant helps ensure that borrowers interested in reAlpha Mortgage automatically receive a timely, topical response to their inquiry. In addition, the system is built for proactive and compliant borrower engagement. It enables timely outreach informed by borrower intent signals and provides consistent follow-up through personalized and brand-aligned conversations. Each interaction is captured in the CRM with full context, giving loan officers visibility into borrower goals and history while maintaining compliance through encryption and audit-ready records. With the internal assistant handling repetitive outreach and pre-qualification tasks, loan officers have more time to focus on what matters most, building relationships and guiding borrowers through successful applications. “Our internal AI-Powered Engagement Assistant is about enabling our people, not replacing them,” said Jamie Cavanaugh, CEO of reAlpha Mortgage. “By automating early interactions, we aim to help ensure that every lead receives timely attention while giving loan officers more capacity to connect directly with borrowers who are ready to move forward. We expect this to lead to faster appointments, less manual work, and an improved experience for both our team and our customers.” “We engineered the system to think, adapt, and scale - giving our loan officers more time for the conversations that matter.” said Vijay Rathna, Chief Technology Officer of reAlpha. “By combining multiple AI agents within a single framework, the system can manage high lead volumes, adapt to borrower needs in real time, and integrate seamlessly with our CRM. We believe that this foundation ensures that our technology not only improves speed and efficiency today, but can also evolve with new capabilities as we expand.” This launch represents the latest addition to reAlpha Mortgage’s AI-enabled product stack. It builds on the earlier launch of the internal AI Loan Officer Assistant, which automates document classification, extraction, and validation for loan officers. The two products are expected to work together to reduce administrative burden, increase operational efficiency, and allow loan officers to focus on building stronger relationships with borrowers. About reAlpha Tech Corp. reAlpha Tech Corp. (Nasdaq: AIRE) is an AI-powered real estate technology company that aims to transform the multi-trillion-dollar U.S. real estate services market. reAlpha is developing an end-to-end platform that streamlines real estate transactions through integrated brokerage, mortgage, and title services. With a strategic, acquisition-driven growth model and proprietary AI infrastructure, reAlpha is building a vertically integrated ecosystem designed to deliver a simpler, smarter, and more affordable path to homeownership. For more information, visit www.realpha.com . title: Best Medical Record Retrieval Integrations for Filevine (2026)
summary: Compare the leading medical record retrieval integrations for Filevine in 2026, including the Codes Health strategic partnership that delivers AI-native retrieval and complete records in a couple of weeks.
body_text: Medical record retrieval has long been the bottleneck that stalls settlements, consumes paralegal hours, and creates trial preparation chaos. Filevine users now have multiple integration options that promise to streamline this workflow, but not all integrations deliver equal value. This guide examines the leading retrieval integrations available for Filevine in 2026, with a particular focus on its partnership with Codes Health, which brings AI-native retrieval directly into your case management environment. Key Takeaways Filevine announced a strategic partnership with Codes Health that embeds AI-native medical record retrieval directly into the Filevine workflow The Filevine-Codes Health integration allows users to submit requests, track status, communicate with the retrieval team, and receive completed records without leaving the Filevine project Traditional retrieval integrations report 15 to 21-day turnaround for standard requests, while AI-powered platforms like Codes Health target a couple of weeks with proactive error prevention EHR-connected services can offer rapid retrieval from supported providers, but coverage and packaging vary by vendor, and firms should confirm whether a given response covers the complete date range, facility, and record type requested Setup complexity ranges from roughly 15 minutes for basic configurations to several hours for custom field mapping, depending on the vendor Integration pricing varies from $45 to $50 per request for traditional services to flat-fee structures for AI-powered platforms. Factor in provider fees and any separate chronology costs when comparing Integrating Medical Records: The Future of Legal Case Management Software Medical record retrieval integrations transform how personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice firms manage case documentation. Rather than toggling between case management platforms, vendor portals, email, and downloaded file folders, modern integrations keep requests and communications associated with the appropriate case file. Filevine functions as a system of record for legal work, connecting matters, documents, contracts, and workflows in a single environment. The right retrieval integration extends this capability by automating request submission, status tracking, and document delivery within that same workspace. What separates integration approaches: Embedded partnerships (like Codes Health) build retrieval directly into the Filevine case workflow, including request submission, status tracking, and communication Native integrations connect through Filevine's API and webhook tools, with the amount of activity that happens inside Filevine versus a separate vendor portal varying by provider Third-party connectors bolt retrieval onto existing workflows with varying levels of automation The distinction that matters most for a firm is how much of the day-to-day workflow, request status, records, and communication actually stay inside Filevine versus require a separate account or portal. 1. Codes Health: Filevine's Partner for AI-Native Retrieval In July 2026, Filevine announced a strategic partnership with Codes Health that goes beyond a standard third-party integration. This partnership embeds AI-native medical record retrieval directly into the Filevine environment where legal teams already manage their cases. How the Integration Works Filevine users can initiate medical record requests from a case file, track status in real time, communicate with the Codes Health team, and receive completed records and billing inside the Filevine project. The workflow is designed to reduce the fragmented process of managing retrieval through a separate vendor portal. Key workflow capabilities: Submit requests directly from the relevant Filevine project AI-powered validation checks authorizations, date ranges, and provider-specific requirements before submission Real-time status tracking provides visibility into provider outreach and follow-up attempts In-platform communication with the Codes Health team without leaving the case file Automatic delivery of completed medical, billing, and imaging records to the Filevine project Completeness verification against the original request before records are returned What Sets Codes Health Apart Codes Health combines a proprietary facility database , AI validation, and an operations layer that follows up until records reach the law firm. Codes Health uses calls, faxes, emails, portals, and automated follow-up workflows to pursue outstanding records while keeping firms informed. AI capabilities that traditional services lack: Proactive error prevention : AI review catches incomplete authorization forms, missing signatures, unclear expiration dates, and unchecked boxes for sensitive records before submission Missing record detection : The system flags gaps in documentation by comparing treatment records to what should exist Automated chronologies : Records arrive organized chronologically across all providers, ready for expert review Case insights extraction : AI identifies buried diagnoses, breaches of care, and documented future expenses The platform targets a couple of weeks for complete records, a significant improvement over traditional manual processes that can stretch from weeks to months. Pricing follows a flat-fee structure; firms should confirm the treatment of provider and copy charges during the sales process. Codes Health was founded in 2024 by graduates of MIT and Yale and is backed by institutional investors, including Y Combinator, Amplify Partners, and Haystack. The company is trusted by hundreds of firms across personal injury, mass tort, and medical malpractice. Codes Health's MIT-educated engineering team continuously builds out additional workflows and products, ensuring the platform constantly evolves and becomes more comprehensive to meet the changing demands of modern legal practices. For high-volume customers, Codes Health can build custom integrations with CRM platforms and other medical software systems to further streamline workflows. 2. Record Retrieval Solutions (RRS) RRS provides a native Filevine integration through their RecordSync portal. The service lists a $45 service fee per request, excluding provider and copy fees, with an average 15-day turnaround. Integration features: Activate directly from Filevine's Advanced menu Real-time status syncing with case files Document auto-filing to the appropriate project folders HIPAA Secure Now (HSN) certified RRS offers retrieval through Filevine and a separate summarization service for chronology and review needs; scope and pricing should be confirmed directly with RRS. 3. YoCierge YoCierge offers rapid EHR retrieval from supported providers, subject to patient authorization and provider availability, falling back to traditional retrieval when EHR access is unavailable. Integration highlights: OAuth connection with the Filevine section import DICOM image upload to the Filevine Documents folder Compatible with Filevine's browser-based DICOM viewer Automatic expense registration in the Filevine cost tab YoCierge reports SOC 2 Type II attestation and ISO 27001 certification AI-assisted chronology and record-analysis products, with packaging and pricing to be confirmed with the vendor Setup complexity: Moderate (30 to 60 minutes). Requires creating Personal Access Tokens and configuring Webhook Subscriptions. Pricing: Volume-based flat fee structure. Codes Health cautions that same-day EHR retrieval can be useful, but firms should verify whether the response covers the complete date range, facility, record type, billing file, and imaging requested. Gaps that surface later can mean additional client involvement and follow-up, which is part of why Codes Health emphasizes completeness review and continued follow-up when records are missing. 4. Records on Time Records on Time provides a dual-mode retrieval approach: EHR access for same-day delivery from a reported 400,000-plus connected providers, with automatic fallback to traditional retrieval (a reported 21-day average) when EHR is unavailable. Key differentiators: $49.95 retrieval fee, plus applicable provider fees for traditional retrieval; its EHR retrieval option is advertised without provider fees A reported 99 percent completion rate Single point of contact for support Best for firms wanting broad EHR coverage with a predictable traditional fallback. 5. Arctrieval Arctrieval is best evaluated as an in-house retrieval workflow platform rather than a managed, full-service retrieval and AI review service. Arctrieval offers two Filevine setup paths: a standard configuration that imports prebuilt .fvst sections, or a custom configuration that manually maps Arctrieval fields into existing Filevine sections. Technical capabilities: Multiple Filevine contact type mappings Sub-folder auto-creation per request Role-based permissions for unlinking records Optional Department field for organizational contacts Setup complexity: Arctrieval estimates approximately 15 minutes for standard configuration when the required permissions are already available. Custom configurations may require an experienced Filevine administrator or integration partner. Best for firms with complex custom workflows requiring granular control over data flow. Integration Comparison: Choosing the Right Option Codes Health: Integration Type: Embedded partnership Setup Time: Handled during onboarding Turnaround: A couple of weeks EHR Same-Day: No AI Analysis: Included AI Chronology: Included Error Prevention: AI-powered Completeness Check: Automated RRS: Integration Type: Native Setup Time: Not publicly specified Turnaround: 15 days (reported) EHR Same-Day: No AI Analysis: Not included AI Chronology: Separate service Error Prevention: Manual review Completeness Check: Manual YoCierge: Integration Type: Native Setup Time: 30 to 60 minutes Turnaround: 21 days (traditional fallback) EHR Same-Day: Yes, for supported providers AI Analysis: Available, packaging varies AI Chronology: Available, packaging varies Error Prevention: Manual review Completeness Check: Manual Records on Time: Integration Type: Native Setup Time: 30 to 60 minutes Turnaround: 21 days (traditional, reported) EHR Same-Day: Yes, from a reported 400,000-plus providers AI Analysis: Not included AI Chronology: Not included Error Prevention: Manual review Completeness Check: Manual Arctrieval: Integration Type: API/Webhook Setup Time: Approximately 15 minutes for standard configuration Turnaround: Contact vendor EHR Same-Day: No AI Analysis: Not included AI Chronology: Not included Error Prevention: Manual review Completeness Check: Manual Decision Framework Choose Codes Health if: You need complete records with AI analysis and expert verification Medical malpractice cases require breach-of-care identification Embedded Filevine workflow benefits matter to your team Proactive missing record detection is critical for your practice areas Choose a traditional integration if: Budget constraints require per-request pricing You have internal paralegal capacity for manual record review Same-day EHR retrieval is valuable for your provider mix Simple setup with minimal configuration is preferred Implementation Best Practices Setup Requirements Requirements vary by vendor. Confirm the necessary Filevine permissions, tokens, templates, and onboarding steps directly with each provider before implementation. Common elements across several vendors include: Admin-level Filevine access for configuration An active retrieval vendor account with the selected provider Personal Access Token generation, where applicable (displayed only once; store immediately in a secure password manager) Configured project templates with imported retrieval sections Common Setup Challenges Personal Access Token lost: Tokens only display once at creation. If lost, generate a new token. The original cannot be recovered. Import/Export tool not visible: Contact Filevine support to enable the Customs Editor import feature before beginning setup. Field mapping errors: Verify exact section/field selector matches between Filevine and the retrieval platform using the vendor's verification tool before going live. Multiple project templates: Import retrieval sections into each template type that requires medical records. Don't assume one template covers all case types. Testing Protocol Submit 2 to 3 test requests across different project template types Verify records auto-file to correct folders with proper naming conventions Check expense tracking flows to the cost tab accurately Test status update sync in the project timeline Confirm communication channels work within the case file (for embedded partnerships) The Total Cost Picture Per-request pricing tells only part of the story. When comparing options, factor in the full cost framework: the base service fee, any provider or copy fees, staff time spent on follow-up and review, chronology or analysis fees, rework from rejected requests, and onboarding effort. Traditional services (RRS, YoCierge, Records on Time): Per-request fee in the $45 to $50 range, plus applicable provider fees Chronology and analysis typically require a separate service or vendor Staff time for manual follow-up and review, which varies by firm and case complexity AI-powered platforms (Codes Health): Flat fee per case Chronologies included as part of the service Reduced staff time on organization and analysis, since AI handles much of that work Confirm the treatment of provider and copy charges during the sales process The actual savings from an integrated AI platform versus traditional retrieval plus a separate chronology service will depend on a firm's case volume, complexity, and current staffing, so firms should model this against their own numbers rather than a generic industry figure. Frequently Asked Questions How long does setup take for Filevine retrieval integrations? Setup complexity varies by integration type and vendor. Arctrieval estimates roughly 15 minutes for standard configuration when permissions are available. Native OAuth integrations like YoCierge and Records on Time typically take 30 to 60 minutes, including token creation and webhook configuration. The Codes Health partnership with Filevine includes onboarding support, with configuration handled during activation. Confirm exact timelines and requirements with each vendor. What's the difference between an embedded partnership and a standard integration? Standard integrations connect two separate platforms via API, and the amount of work that happens inside a separate vendor portal versus inside Filevine varies by provider. The Codes Health-Filevine partnership goes beyond standard integration by embedding retrieval capabilities directly into Filevine. Users can submit requests, track status, communicate, and receive records without leaving their case file. Do I need a separate chronology service with these integrations? Some traditional retrieval services deliver raw records that require separate chronology creation through a third-party vendor or internal paralegal time. Codes Health includes AI chronologies as part of its service, delivering records organized with extracted case insights. Can general AI tools like ChatGPT analyze my medical records? General-purpose AI should not be treated as a substitute for a purpose-built legal medical record platform. Some enterprise AI products can support HIPAA-regulated use in the right configuration, but users still need appropriate agreements, controls, validation, and human review before relying on the output for litigation. Codes Health's platform combines AI analysis with human expert verification, a hybrid model designed to support accuracy for case preparation while delivering speed advantages over manual review. What causes most medical record request rejections? Codes Health identifies incomplete authorizations as a leading cause of denied requests. Missing patient signatures, unclear expiration dates, or unchecked boxes for sensitive records can require resubmission and restart the applicable provider processing period. (Provider or vendor workflows sometimes use an internal window of about 15 days, though the general HIPAA right-of-access rule gives covered entities up to 30 calendar days to respond, subject to limited extensions.) Codes Health's AI review catches these errors before submission, automatically flagging misspellings, missing dates of service, and signature issues that would otherwise cause provider rejections.
